classification.difficultyReason: Infer the vertical separation from the two contour heights, put it and the direct distance in matching units, then identify opposite and hypotenuse and apply inverse sine.

content.prompt: Two bushwalkers, Gore and Tess, are testing new electronic measuring devices. Gore is on a mountain side at the $2300\text{ m}$ contour line. Tess is at the $2150\text{ m}$ contour line on a different mountain. Their measuring devices say that the direct distance between them is $1.35\text{ km}$. Find the angle of elevation, correct to 2 decimal places, from Tess to Gore.

answer.short:
$6.38^\circ$

Use the vertical separation and direct distance in the sine ratio.
answer.worked:
The vertical separation is $2300-2150=150\text{ m}$, and the direct distance is $1.35\text{ km}=1350\text{ m}$. Let $\theta$ be the angle of elevation from Tess to Gore.

$$\begin{align*}\sin\theta&=\frac{150}{1350}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{1}{9}\\\theta&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)\\\theta&\approx6.38^\circ\end{align*}$$
